Source: the selected node's supplied proof (class_reduction), which follows Simon 7.3.3, Remark 3.4 and the proof of 3.3(2) (chapter-07.txt lines 380–398 and 512–583) and Appendix A, A.1–A.4 (chapter-A.txt lines 18–45). This child is step 2 of that proof ("Normalization": (a), (b), (c)) together with the local integrability part of step 5 ((H1)).
1. (The constant.) By euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def, on every Euclid P, μHE[n] = a•μH[n] with a := addHaarScalarFactor(volume on Euclid n, μH[n] on Euclid n) ∈ ℝ≥0. a depends only on n. By addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero, a ≠ 0, and a < ∞ because a ∈ ℝ≥0. Put c := (a : ℝ)⁻¹ > 0. Fix Q, μ, g, e satisfying the hypotheses.
2. (Lower integrals.) For a Borel set A and a Borel h : ℝ^P → [0, ∞], ∫⁻_A h dμHE[n] = a·∫⁻_A h dμH[n] (Measure.restrict_smul, lintegral_smul_measure). By withDensity_apply, μ(A) = ∫⁻_A ofReal(g) dμHE[n] = a·∫⁻_A ofReal(g) dμH[n]. Since a ∈ (0, ∞), ∫⁻_A ofReal(g) dμH[n] = a⁻¹·μ(A).
3. ((i) local integrability.) g is Borel, so x ↦ g(x)•e is Borel (Measurable.smul_const). Euclid Q is second countable, so this map is strongly measurable and in particular a.e. strongly measurable for μH[n]. Fix x ∈ ℝ^P and use the neighbourhood B_1(x) ∈ 𝓝 x. Since g ≥ 0, ‖g(z)•e‖ₑ = ofReal(g(z))·‖e‖ₑ. Step 2 gives ∫⁻_{B_1(x)} ‖g•e‖ₑ dμH[n] = ‖e‖ₑ·a⁻¹·μ(B_1(x)) ≤ ‖e‖ₑ·a⁻¹·μ(closedBall x 1) < ∞, because closedBall x 1 is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and μ is finite on compact sets. So g•e is integrable on a neighbourhood of every point, i.e. LocallyIntegrable (g•e) μH[n]. Equivalently, by locallyIntegrable_iff it suffices that g•e be integrable on every compact K; the same computation with K in place of B_1(x) bounds the lower integral (hasFiniteIntegral_iff_ofReal), and Integrable.smul_const handles e.
4. ((ii), pulling out e.) Fix f. f(x)•(g(x)•e) = (f(x)g(x))•e (smul_smul), and integral_smul_const gives ∫ f(x)•(g(x)•e) dμH[n] = (∫ f g dμH[n])•e. This holds whether or not f g is μH[n]-integrable. If it is not and e ≠ 0, then x ↦ (f(x)g(x))•e is not integrable either, so both sides are 0. If e = 0, both sides are 0.
5. (From μH[n] to μHE[n].) integral_smul_nnreal_measure (or integral_smul_measure with the coercion of a) gives ∫ f g dμHE[n] = ∫ f g d(a•μH[n]) = a·∫ f g dμH[n]. Since a ≠ 0, ∫ f g dμH[n] = a⁻¹·∫ f g dμHE[n].
6. (From μHE[n] to μ.) ofReal(g(x)) = ((g x).toNNReal : [0, ∞]) by definition of ENNReal.ofReal, and x ↦ (g x).toNNReal is measurable. integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul gives ∫ f dμ = ∫ f d(μHE[n].withDensity(x ↦ (g x).toNNReal)) = ∫ (g x).toNNReal • f(x) dμHE[n] = ∫ g f dμHE[n], using ((g x).toNNReal : ℝ) = g(x) since g ≥ 0. This identity is unconditional.
7. (Conclusion.) Steps 4–6 give ∫ f(x)•(g(x)•e) dμH[n] = (a⁻¹·∫ f dμ)•e = (c·∫ f dμ)•e. Steps 3 and 7 prove (i) and (ii) with the constant c of step 1, which depends only on n. ∎
